title: Compositional concepts
source: Rector, PEN&PAD, GALEN & GRAIL, DRAFT Nov 2026, pp. 3–4, §4.1 and §5.1.

steps.title: A lesion is already a composition
steps.body: Many OpenGALEN names are compositions that were written out and given a name. InflammationLesion is one: a pathological structure tied to an inflammation process. The next step uses that name inside another definition.
steps.dump: In this dump the definition is “PathologicalBodyStructure which hasUniqueAssociatedProcess InflammationProcess”. InflammationLesion is the same concept as InflammatoryLesion.

steps.title: Pericarditis names one composition
steps.body: Pericarditis is not a further primitive. Its definition takes InflammationLesion and locates it in the pericardium. The draft’s shorter wording, “Inflammation of the Pericardium”, is the same example under generic labels. Those shorter words are not the concept names here.
steps.task: Read the definition, then follow hasSpecificLocation to Pericardium if you want the part.

quote.text: Definitions – Pericarditis = Inflammation of the Pericardium

steps.dump: In this dump the definition is “InflammationLesion which hasSpecificLocation Pericardium”.

steps.title: Thumb names another
steps.body: Thumb, also named Pollux, is the composition of Finger with the ordinal value first. The previous chapter’s sanction on Digit is what made that role sensible to use. This step is only the named result.
steps.dump: In this dump the definition is “Finger which hasOrdinalPosition first”.

steps.title: A nested laterality, and the draft’s thumb
steps.body: The draft’s dislocation of a right thumb is written with generic labels. No concept has that wording. RightLaterality is not a concept, and Dislocation is not a concept. What this dump does have is a named, nested laterality, and a named dislocation of a joint.
steps.task: Read the definition of the concept on screen. The nested selector is hasLeftRightSelector leftSelection.

quote.text: (Dislocation that hasLocation some (Thumb that hasLaterality some RightLaterality)

steps.dump: In this dump, ChestPainRadiatingToLeftArm is “ChestPain which isActedOnBy (PainRadiation which hasUniqueAssociatedDisplacement (Displacement which isDisplacementTo (Arm which hasLeftRightSelector leftSelection)))”. JointDislocation is “DislocationLesion which hasSpecificLocation Joint”. hasLocation is a property name here; this dislocation definition uses hasSpecificLocation. hasLaterality is not a property name; hasLeftRightSelector is. rightSelection exists, and this named pain uses leftSelection. The draft’s labels are the generic ones Alan Rector said came from more general papers (November 2026, personal communication to Erik).

steps.title: Post-coordination was dynamic
steps.body: Applying a code to a patient situation, in the draft’s account, says that the situation is a member of a class. There cannot be a permanent class for every situation. GALEN’s approach was to build a post-coordinated class at the time of recording, classify it, and not keep that class in the model. This page has no classifier. It can show a composition only when the composition was already given a name, as with the concept still open from the previous step.
steps.task: Nothing to compose. There is no box here that classifies a new expression.

quotes.text: to apply a code to a patient situation is to say that that situation is a member of the corresponding class.
Producing class/concepts/terms for every possible patient situation is impossible.
neither the code nor the class was made a permanent part of the model because the model would rapidly have become too large to manage.

steps.dump: In this dump the named compositions above are ordinary concepts. A new expression that is not already a name cannot be classified on this page.
